t: You're standing by the Laboratory Building at New River Head, in Islington. It was designed by John Murray Easton, a Scottish architect born in 1889 who died in 1975. Easton won the Royal Gold Medal for architecture, awarded by the Royal Institute of British Architects, which is among the highest honours in the profession. That recognition is the reason his name matters here, and it tells you this building came from a respected hand.
